pluss::note::rand¶

Back to Note Factory API Reference

Signatures¶

Note pluss::note::rand(integer_range sizes, bool capitalize = true,
                       std::uint64_t seed = 0)
Note pluss::note::rand(std::initializer_list<std::int64_t> sizes,
                       bool capitalize = true, std::uint64_t seed = 0)

One Random Letter Per Cell¶

rand() allocates a Note of shape sizes and fills each cell with a single random letter drawn uniformly from the 26-letter English alphabet. It is the text counterpart of pluss::series::rand — a quick source of throwaway data shaped exactly how you need it, for tests, fixtures, placeholder tables, and examples.

Every cell is an independent draw of one character. rand does not build words or syllables; for random words, draw letters and join, or use a domain-specific generator.

Parameters¶

  • sizes — the output shape, same rules as full: an initializer_list (no wrapper needed) or any contiguous std::int64_t range, empty for a scalar, non-negative extents, rank at most three.

  • capitalize — true (default) draws from A–Z; false draws from a–z.

  • seed — the PRNG seed. A non-zero seed makes the draw fully deterministic: the same seed, sizes, and capitalize always produce the same Note. A seed of 0 (the default) is drawn from a process-wide entropy source, so each call differs — use 0 for genuine scratch data, a fixed non-zero value whenever the output must be reproducible (tests, documented examples).

The result is UTF-8 mode. Filling n cells uses storage proportional to n.

Example 1: A Seeded Row Of Capitals¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::note::rand({6}, true, 42)) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[6], dim=1, numel=6, encoding=utf8)
["W", "I", "K", "O", "V", "A"]

Six independent draws from A–Z. Seed 42 fixes the sequence.

Example 2: The Same Seed Reproduces The Same Draw¶

const pluss::Note again = pluss::note::rand({6}, true, 42);
std::cout << again << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[6], dim=1, numel=6, encoding=utf8)
["W", "I", "K", "O", "V", "A"]

Identical to Example 1 — a non-zero seed is a reproducibility guarantee.

Example 3: Lower-Case Letters¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::note::rand({6}, false, 42)) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[6], dim=1, numel=6, encoding=utf8)
["w", "i", "k", "o", "v", "a"]

capitalize = false draws from a–z. With the same seed the letter positions in the alphabet match Example 1, lower-cased.

Example 4: A Two-Dimensional Block¶

const pluss::Note n = pluss::note::rand({2, 4}, true, 7);
pluss::note::print(std::cout, n) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 4], dim=2, numel=8, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["H", "C", "O", "W"], 
  ["M", "B", "G", "B"]
]

Any rank up to three; the draw order follows row-major cell order.

Example 5: A Scalar Draw¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::note::rand({}, true, 99)) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"D"

An empty sizes list gives a single-cell scalar Note.

See Also¶

  • pluss::note::rand_between: random single characters from an arbitrary ASCII range, not just letters.

  • pluss::note::arange: a deterministic stepped run instead of a random draw.

  • pluss::note::full: fill a shape with one fixed value.
